name: Flower Colour Preference
description:
Faithful replication of the online survey in She, Wu, Pi, Huang & Bao (2025), Horticulturae 11:54. Participants see 29 pictures of the same Zephyranthes 'Lily Pies' flower bed: the original pink photograph, 15 other single colours (blue, turquoise, green, white, red, orange, purple, yellow and deep variants) and 13 mixes of two light colours. Each picture is rated from 1 (strongly dislike) to 6 (strongly like). Before the pictures they answer the paper's questions on sex, age, residential area, household income, personal income sources, education and how often they visit small parks, large parks and nature. Each trial records whether the picture is a single colour or a two-colour mix and which colours. Analysis: mean flower colour rating per picture; preference against the CIELAB L*, a*, b* values of each colour (paper Table A2) with a generalized additive model; age, income, nature experience and mood as drivers (paper: blue, deep blue, turquoise and white liked most; white with blue the best mix).

Pictures: the 29 samples printed in the paper's Figure 2 (CC BY 4.0). The original photograph was taken by the authors and the other colours were made by hand by changing only the flower colour with Photoshop colour curves (no generative tools). Used with credit; the template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) the paper measured mood with the 40-item Profile of Mood States short form (POMS); this copyrighted questionnaire is left out, so the mood analysis cannot be repeated without adding a licensed mood measure; (2) the paper ran on the Wenjuanxing platform in China; the questions here are in English and the income bands are in Chinese yuan as in the paper; (3) occupation (more than 18 categories, not listed in the paper) is not asked; (4) pictures are cropped from the published figure without the colour scales printed beside them.

elements.title: Rate this picture from 1 to 6.
elements.description: 29 pictures (paper Figure 2): 16 single-colour flowers (the original pink photo of Zephyranthes 'Lily Pies' and 15 colours made by changing only the flower colour with Photoshop colour curves) and 13 mixes of two light colours; each on its own page in random order. One trial per picture (key = file name), values preference (1 = strongly dislike, 6 = strongly like), picture, flower_type (single colour / two colours), colour, position. Analysis in the paper: mean flower colour rating (FCR) per picture; GAM of preference against CIELAB L*, a*, b* of each colour (paper Table A2); random forest and piecewise SEM with age, income, personal income sources, nature experience and mood (POMS total mood disturbance).
